claims.claim: **Take a detailed drug allergy history** to guide the antibiotic choice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid drugs from both β-lactam classes after an immediate or severe reaction to either one (penicillin or cephalosporin).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-immediate and non-severe reaction: an antibiotic from the alternate β-lactam class can be prescribed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test for drug allergy (by drug challenge or skin testing) only in controlled settings.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Up to a quarter of children presenting to hospital report an antibiotic allergy. **Over 90% of children whose β-lactam reaction was non-immediate tolerate a re-challenge** with the same drug.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Three quarters of children who identify as penicillin-allergic do so by 3 years of age.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timing:** symptoms under 1 hour after ingestion = **immediate**; over 1 hour = **delayed**. Record the duration of symptoms and time to recovery.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type of reaction:** rash (non-specific, maculopapular, urticarial) · respiratory symptoms (wheeze, stridor, increased work of breathing) · collapse or dizziness · angioedema of the airway (mouth, eyes, lips, tongue) · involvement of mucous membranes · gastrointestinal symptoms · muscle and joint pain · whether immediate treatment was needed (adrenaline auto-injector, bronchodilator) · previous anaphylaxis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also record:** concurrent drugs · concurrent illness (e.g. possible viral infection) · **antibiotics tolerated since, especially after the reported reaction** · other allergies, drug and non-drug · atopic disease. No specific examination is required.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immediate (<1 hour), severe** (anaphylaxis, bronchospasm or airway angioedema): **do not give any drug from the same β-lactam class, or any with potential for cross-reactivity.** **Immediate, non-severe** (e.g. isolated urticaria, pruritus): may consider a non-cross-reactive drug from the alternate β-lactam class.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delayed (>1 hour) reaction with a suspected SCAR (severe cutaneous adverse reaction): avoid all β-lactams.** SCARs include Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS and acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis. **Cytopenias, or acute kidney injury or drug-induced liver injury:** discuss with the local paediatric team or drug allergy service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Delayed reactions: all non-β-lactam antibiotics, or aztreonam, are safe to prescribe.** Non-severe delayed reactions (e.g. pruritus or isolated exanthem): **a β-lactam from the alternative class is safe.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timing unknown:** treat a severe reaction as immediate-severe, and a non-severe reaction as delayed-non-severe.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer for drug allergy assessment and document the allergy** in the medical record pending the outcome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unlikely allergy** — known drug side effects (e.g. nausea, headache) or a family history only: **all β-lactams are safe; remove the drug allergy label.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: When a child has reacted immediately to a cephalosporin or penicillin, **cross-reactivity is most likely with a β-lactam that shares its R1 side chain.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected allergy to amoxicillin or ampicillin: do not use cefalexin or cefaclor**, unless the reaction was non-immediate and non-severe.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected ceftriaxone allergy: avoid cefotaxime and cefepime.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin–carbapenem cross-reactivity (e.g. imipenem, meropenem) is rare — around 1%.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team:** a clear history of an immediate or severe antibiotic allergy in any child; a non-severe reaction in a child who needs urgent or ongoing antibiotics. **Immediate and non-immediate reactions alike can go to an outpatient allergy clinic** for formal assessment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
